Hi all — notes and a small workbook attached (redwood_reserve_sku_matrix.xlsx). Key points below, kept compact for procurement: 

- Recommended reserve SKUs: For mixed chat+embed+rerank at your target, we recommend a base reserved pool of H100-80GB (for chat P95 latency headroom) plus A100-40GB as the workhorse for embeddings and reranking. L40s are cost-efficient for high-volume quantized embeddings but less predictable for long-context chat.

- Throughput ballpark (quantized 4-bit) at 8k context, single-replica estimates (P50 / P95 tail-latency):
  • H100-80GB: chat gen (gpt-like decoder): 160 tks/s (P50) / 85 tks/s (P95) on our optimized kernels.
  • A100-40GB: chat gen: 110 tks/s (P50) / 60 tks/s (P95).
  • L40s: chat gen: 95 tks/s (P50) / 50 tks/s (P95) — better at embeddings, less so at large-context chattiness.

- Reservation packing and suggested mix (for 200 qps steady, 600 qps burst):
  • Base reserve: 6x H100 + 8x A100 (assumes sharding & multiplexing; see workbook numbers). Reserve handles steady + moderate burst (2.5x).
  • On-demand/spot: L40s + additional A100s for ephemeral spikes to 3x.

- Tail-runway (72-hour spike) guardrails:
  1) Pre-book a 30% burst pool (on Dedicated) that can be activated for 72h at pre-agreed price.
  2) Auto-fallback policy: route traffic to quantized variants and shorter contexts once tail-latency crosses threshold — we can tier routes (H100-primary, A100-secondary, L40s-quantized-fallback).
  3) Credit buffer: recommend a financial buffer equal to 50% of monthly committed spend to cover a single 72-hour 3x event (workbook models alternate buffers: 30% / 50% / 75%).

I'll highlight the specific cost deltas in the spreadsheet. If Aurelia needs microbench builds (their model + tokens), we can run a 2-hour sample in our staging fleet and include traces.

Attachment: redwood_reserve_sku_matrix.xlsx

— Kimberly

Tom — thanks for the concise asks. See inline summary below and attached one-page PDF for procurement. High level: we split your needs into three scenarios (Conservative, Baseline, Aggressive) with SKU mixes and cost deltas. The workbook has the packing math; highlights follow: 

1) SKU mix recommendation (Baseline): Reserve H100-80GB (6 units) + A100-40GB (8 units). Use L40s for on-demand burst and embedding offload. This mix balances latency SLOs and unit cost.

2) 72-hour spike plan: pre-authorize a burst pool equivalent to 30% of reserved vCPU-hours with automated activation. If you prefer contractual guarantee, a short-term Burst Addendum (72–168 hours) is available at a fixed uplift.

3) Throughput & tail-latency numbers: Kimberly attached the numbers (quartiles) from our internal bench. Those are conservative; we recommend running a 2-hour pilot using a sanitized model trace to validate. If agreeable, we can schedule the pilot next week.

Action items / next steps: 
- Procurement: review attached summary PDF and the workbook (redwood_reserve_sku_matrix.xlsx).
- Engineering: approve a 2-hour pilot (Marcus to coordinate).
- Commercial: we can draft Burst Addendum wording (if Aurelia wants guaranteed burst).

Attached: redwood_rfi_response_summary.pdf, redwood_reserve_sku_matrix.xlsx
